correctness.rationale: The finite-difference argument applied to F(x)=binom((n-1)x,n-1) yields D(n-1)|n. At each prime p^a||n, the Kummer residue/carry count gives the uniform lower bound a-b, with b=floor(log_p(n/p^a)), by counting the first a carries and the extra a+h carries when v_p(q-1)>b; the explicit multiplier q=1+p^a(m-p^b), or q=2 for m=1, yields exactly a-b carries, with the published Guo et al. Lemma 9 handling zero valuation when m>p^a. Independently used Legendre factorial valuations over every q=2..n for n=3..349: 680 local prime checks, all exact; tested 313 nonzero-val minimizer witnesses. The theorem is exactly for n>=3 and q in this finite window.
